questions.question: Differentiate between toxic and corrosive chemicals? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between toxic and corrosive chemicals?
  • Answer: Toxic chemicals are those harmful to living organisms or tissues by intake or absorption into the
  • body by means of consumption, inhaling. These may cause damage to the internal organs and other functional
  • systems like nervous system or digestive system. Eg. lead, mercury, arsenic, chloroform etc.
  • Corrosive chemicals are those chemicals which causes destruction on tissues which comes under
  • direct contact. It may causes burn, itching etc. at the point of contact and the effect may be rapid. Eg. sulfuric
  • acid, hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide etc. Corrosive chemicals can destroy not only tissues but materials
  • like plastics, metals etc. as well.
  • (Any other relevant explanation in 2-3 sentences for each with examples can be given full marks)

questions.question: Describe with a diagram the main parts of a bullet and their composition. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe with a diagram the main parts of a bullet and their composition
  • The major components of bullets are
  • (a)Case:- The container that holds all the other ammunition com ponents together. It’s usually made of brass,
  • steel, copper, paper, or plastic.
  • (b)Gunpowder:- A chemical mixture that burns rapidly and converts to an expanding gas when ignited.
  • (c)Primer:- An explosive chemical compound that ignites the gunpowder when struck by a firing pin. Primer
  • may be placed either in the rim of the case (rimfire) or in the center of the base of the case (centerfire).
  • (d)Projectile: The bullet is the actual projectile that leaves the end of the barrel and moves towards the target.
  • (Diagram – 3 marks. Reasonable explanation of at least 3 parts – 4 marks)

questions.question: Explain the application of ultraviolet rays in forensic document examination with at least four examples. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the application of ultraviolet rays in forensic document examination with at least four examples.
  • Answer:
  • ▪ Detection of altered inks: Different inks fluoresce differently under UV light, helping to identify additions
  • or modifications.
  • ▪ Identification of erasures: Erased or rubbed areas often appear as dull or discolored patches under UV
  • light due to damage to paper fibers.
  • ▪ Distinguishing between original and added entries: UV light can reveal differences in ink used for original
  • text and later additions or corrections.
  • ▪ Detection of invisible ink: Some forgers use invisible ink that can be detected only under UV light.
  • ▪ Verification of security features: UV light reveals hidden security features like UV-fluorescent fibers,
  • threads, and seals in currency, cheques, and official documents.
  • ▪ Detection of washed documents: Chemical washing used to remove original writing leaves traces visible
  • under UV light.
